children.name: Artamella
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga endemic to Madagascar, containing the White-headed Vanga. It has a striking white head contrasting with black wings and tail, and a relatively slender, straight bill adapted for gleaning insects from foliage. It is a social species often seen in small groups.

children.name: Artamella viridis
children.description: The white-headed vanga (Artamella viridis) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Artamella. It is endemic to Madagascar, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Calicalicus
children.description: A genus of small, sexually dimorphic vangas endemic to Madagascar, with males sporting bright red or chestnut patches on the wings and tail. They are among the smallest members of the vanga family and are active, acrobatic foragers in the forest canopy. Their short, stout bills are adapted for gleaning insects from foliage rather than the specialised foraging of other vangas.

children.name: Calicalicus madagascariensis
children.description:
The red-tailed vanga (Calicalicus madagascariensis) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to Madagascar.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Calicalicus rufocarpalis
children.description: The red-shouldered vanga is a member of the vanga family endemic to south-west Madagascar.

children.name: Cyanolanius
children.description: A monotypic genus of strikingly coloured vanga with brilliant azure-blue upperparts that are unique among Malagasy passerines. It has a relatively slender, straight bill and is more of a canopy insectivore than other vangas. Its distribution extends beyond Madagascar to the Comoros Islands, unusual for the family, which is otherwise entirely restricted to Madagascar.

children.name: Cyanolanius comorensis
children.description: The Comoros blue vanga or Comoro blue vanga is a bird species in the family Vangidae. It is found in the Comoros, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Cyanolanius madagascarinus
children.description: The Madagascar blue vanga (Cyanolanius madagascarinus) is a bird species in the family Vangidae. It is found in Madagascar, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Euryceros
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the extraordinary Helmet Vanga, one of the most distinctive birds in Madagascar. It has a massive, deep, laterally compressed bill that is a vivid blue-grey and forms a prominent casque on the forehead. This remarkable adaptation is used to crush large insects and other prey. It is a large, robust vanga of eastern rainforests.

children.name: Euryceros prevostii
children.description: The helmet vanga (Euryceros prevostii) is a distinctive-looking bird of the vanga family, Vangidae, and is classified in its own genus, Euryceros.

children.name: Falculea
children.description: A monotypic vanga genus containing the Sickle-billed Vanga, which possesses the most extreme bill morphology in the family: a long, slender, strongly decurved bill resembling a sickle. This highly specialised tool is used to probe deep into tree crevices and bark furrows for large insects. Endemic to Madagascar, it is the largest species in the vanga family.

children.name: Falculea palliata
children.description: The sickle-billed vanga (Falculea palliata) is a species of bird in the vanga family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Falculea. It is endemic to Madagascar. Its natural habitats are tropical dry forests and tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Hypositta
children.description: A monotypic genus of small vanga containing the Nuthatch Vanga, which convergently resembles a nuthatch in both morphology and behaviour. It has a short, straight bill and strong feet, and is unique among vangas for its tree-creeping foraging style, spiralling up trunks and branches in search of insects. Endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Hypositta corallirostris
children.description: The nuthatch vanga (Hypositta corallirostris), also known as the coral-billed nuthatch-vanga and formerly as the coral-billed nuthatch, is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Leptopterus
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing the Chabert Vanga, a small, pale-eyed species endemic to Madagascar. It has a relatively slender, straight bill and is an active canopy insectivore, often joining mixed-species flocks. Its pale blue-grey plumage makes it one of the more subtly coloured vangas.

children.name: Leptopterus chabert
children.description: Leptopterus chabert (Chabert Vanga) is a vangas species found in Africa region.

children.name: Mystacornis
children.description: A monotypic genus of terrestrial vanga endemic to Madagascar, containing Crossley's Vanga. It has a long, slender, slightly decurved bill and strong legs, adapted for a ground-foraging lifestyle in the leaf litter of the forest floor. It is one of the most secretive and poorly known members of the vanga family.

children.name: Mystacornis crossleyi
children.description: Crossley's vanga (Mystacornis crossleyi), also known as Crossley's babbler-vanga, Crossley's babbler, Madagascar groundhunter, or Madagascar groundjumper, is a bird species in the family Vangidae. It is named after the specimen collector Alfred Crossley.

children.name: Newtonia
children.description: A genus of small, warbler-like vangas endemic to Madagascar, with relatively slender, pointed bills and active foraging styles. They were traditionally placed in the Old World warbler family Sylviidae before molecular studies revealed their true affinities within the vanga family. They are insectivorous birds of forest and scrub habitats.

children.name: Newtonia amphichroa
children.description: The dark newtonia (Newtonia amphichroa) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Newtonia archboldi
children.description:
Archbold's newtonia (Newtonia archboldi) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to Madagascar. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland. The birds have a greyish brown back and tail, with a rufous forecrown and a buffy white belly, throat, and undertail coverts. They have a conspicuous rufous eye-ring, accompanied with a black bill and pale yellow eyes. The species is sexually monomorphic, and there is no major difference between the sexes. There is no breeding plumage for the males.
The newtonia is an insectivore and feeds almost entirely on arthropods. Food is typically gleaned from twigs and foliage, or less commonly from bark or from the ground. It builds an open cup nest which are supported on shrubs. Clutches are typically of 3 eggs. The eggs are reddish white in colour and have many pale brown spots on the larger end of the egg.

children.name: Newtonia brunneicauda
children.description: The common newtonia (Newtonia brunneicauda) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Newtonia fanovanae
children.description:
The red-tailed newtonia (Newtonia fanovanae) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to Madagascar.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Newtonia larvata
children.description: A masked newtonia of the Comoro Islands.

children.name: Newtonia lavarambo
children.description: The dark newtonia is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to northeastern Madagascar. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Newtonia micrura
children.description: A very small vanga with short tail, found in dry forests of western Madagascar.

children.name: Oriolia
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing Bernier's Vanga, a striking black-and-white species endemic to Madagascar. It has a stout, slightly hooked bill and a distinctive white wing patch. It is a forest-dwelling insectivore that forages actively in the canopy, often in mixed-species flocks.

children.name: Oriolia bernieri
children.description: Bernier's vanga (Oriolia bernieri) is a bird species in the family Vangidae. It is in the monotypic genus Oriolia. It is endemic to Madagascar. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Oryzoborus
children.description: A genus of seed-eating birds formerly placed in the tanager family.

children.name: Oryzoborus angolensis
children.description: Oryzoborus angolensis (Chestnut-bellied Seed-finch) is a vangas species found in South America region.

children.name: Pseudobias
children.description: Pseudobias — a genus in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Pseudobias wardi
children.description: Ward's vanga, also known as Ward's flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Pseudobias. It is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Pseudocossyphus
children.description: Small vangas from Madagascar.

children.name: Pseudocossyphus sharpei
children.description: Pseudocossyphus sharpei (Sharpe's Rock Thrush) is a vangas species found in Africa region.

children.name: Pseudocossyphus bensoni
children.description: Pseudocossyphus bensoni (Benson's Rock Thrush) is a vangas species found in Africa region.

children.name: Schetba
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing the Rufous Vanga, a medium-sized, sexually dimorphic species endemic to Madagascar. The male is strikingly coloured with a rufous back and head, while the female is more subdued. It has a relatively stout bill and forages actively in the forest mid-storey.

children.name: Schetba rufa
children.description: The rufous vanga (Schetba rufa) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Tephrodornis
children.description: Tephrodornis — a genus in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Tephrodornis affinis
children.description: The Sri Lanka woodshrike is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is found on Sri Lanka. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the common woodshrike.

children.name: Tephrodornis pondicerianus
children.description: The common woodshrike is a species of bird found in Asia. It is now usually considered a member of the family Vangidae. It is small and ashy brown with a dark cheek patch and a broad white brow.

children.name: Tephrodornis sylvicola
children.description: The Malabar woodshrike is a species of bird usually placed in the family Vangidae. It is found in western India. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the large woodshrike.

children.name: Tephrodornis virgatus
children.description: The large woodshrike is found in south-eastern Asia, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo. Its natural habitats are temperate forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Tylas
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga.

children.name: Tylas albicollis
children.description: A striking black-and-white vanga from eastern Madagascar.

children.name: Tylas eduardi
children.description: The tylas vanga is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Tylas. It is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Vanga
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Hook-billed Vanga, the namesake of the vanga family, endemic to Madagascar. It has a thick, strongly hooked bill that is distinctly crossed at the tip, an adaptation for extracting prey from tree crevices. It is a medium-sized, boldly patterned bird with a black-and-white plumage that makes it easily identifiable in the Malagasy forests.

children.name: Vanga curvirostris
children.description:
The hook-billed vanga (Vanga curvirostris) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to Madagascar. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
In 1760 the French zoologist Mathurin Jacques Brisson included a description of the hook-billed vanga in his Ornithologie based on a specimen collected on the island of Madagascar. He used the French name L'écorcheur de Madagascar and the Latin Collurio Madagascariensis. Although Brisson coined Latin names, these do not conform to the binomial system and are not recognised by the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature. When in 1766 the Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus updated his Systema Naturae for the twelfth edition, he added 240 species that had been previously described by Brisson. One of these was the hook-billed vanga. Linnaeus included a brief description, coined the binomial name Lanius curvirostris and cited Brisson's work. It is now the only species placed in the genus Vanga that was introduced by the French ornithologist Louis Pierre Vieillot in 1816.

children.name: Xenopirostris
children.description: A genus of three medium-sized vangas endemic to Madagascar, characterised by a laterally compressed, blade-like bill that is unique among birds. This remarkable adaptation is used to peel bark and pry into crevices in search of prey. They inhabit dry forests and are among the most specialised foragers in the vanga family.

children.name: Xenopirostris polleni
children.description: Pollen's vanga (Xenopirostris polleni) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to eastern Madagascar. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Xenopirostris xenopirostris
children.description:
Lafresnaye's vanga (Xenopirostris xenopirostris) is a species of bird in the vanga family Vangidae. The species is monotypic and one of three species in the genus Xenopirostris. It is endemic to the south and south west of Madagascar. It inhabits sub-arid thorn scrub, in the Madagascar spiny forests ecoregion, particularly areas with large amounts of dead wood, from sea level. The species has a small range is not common within that range. It was uplisted from Least Concern to Near Threatened in 2022 as it is experiencing moderately rapid population decline owing to habitat degradation and loss within its range.
The common name for the species is derived from the French ornithologist who described it, Frédéric de Lafresnaye. The specific name notes the resemblance of the bill (rostris) to the genus Xenops.

children.name: Xenopirostris damii
children.description:
Van Dam's vanga (Xenopirostris damii) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is endemic to Madagascar.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests. Males may be identified by their black hood whereas females have only a black cap.
